proposals.impact: reduce zero-start drop-off on quiz intro screen
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, two sessions reached the quiz intro screen and neither one clicked to start. Starts are zero. The drop happens before question one, which points to friction on the intro screen itself, not quiz fatigue. Both sessions landed on the intro and left.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is losing every single visitor before they answer anything. The most common cause at this stage is a CTA label or surrounding copy that feels like a commitment before the person knows what they are committing to. Change the start button label and the one sentence directly above it to lower the perceived cost of clicking. The new copy names what happens in the next two minutes in plain terms, with no inflated promise attached.
proposals.new_text:
Answer 10 questions (about 2 minutes)

The questions ask how you actually behave with money, not how you think you should. There are no right answers.

proposals.impact: capitalise on 66.67% open rate with a stronger next-step prompt
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three running sequences at 66.67% (8 opens from 12 sent). Money Avoidance is at 52.63% and Money Worship sits at 37.5%. Vigilance readers are clearly engaged, yet the data shows no downstream conversion signal tied to this sequence. That engagement is not being directed anywhere.
proposals.proposal: Email sequences with strong open rates are warm audiences. The Money Vigilance sequence is the warmest Joel has right now. If the first or second email in that sequence ends with a generic sign-off or a soft "get in touch" line, that is the conversion loss point. Add one specific, low-pressure next step at the close of the first email in the sequence. The step should name what the reader would gain from booking a discovery call in a way that is honest about the work involved, not promotional about the outcome.
proposals.current_text: If any of this resonates, feel free to reply to this email or visit the website to find out more.
proposals.new_text: If you want to look at what your vigilance is actually protecting, a discovery call is where that conversation starts. proposals.impact: convert blog readers to quiz starters
proposals.observation: A new blog post published today: "Why do I trust random advice online more than my own money judgement?" This title maps directly onto the emotional state of someone considering taking the quiz but hesitating. The quiz itself is the behavioural tool that gives a person a grounded read on their own patterns. The post currently has no internal link pointing toward the quiz.
proposals.proposal: A reader who finishes that post is in exactly the right frame of mind to start the quiz. They have just sat with the question of why they distrust their own financial thinking. The quiz is the practical answer. Add one sentence near the end of the post, after the main argument lands, that names the quiz honestly and links to it. Do not frame it as a fix. Frame it as a way to look at the pattern the post just described.
